title: Cool Flame Investigation (CFI)
abstract: The CFI experiments are conceived as follow-up experiments to the FLEX and FLEX-2 droplet combustion experiments onboard the ISS to further explore quasi-steady 'cool flames' controlled by low-temperature chemistry in the NTC region of n-alkane fuels (temperatures 700 to 900 K, vs >1200 K for hot flames). Three fuel combinations were investigated—pure n-dodecane, n-dodecane/iso-dodecane mixtures, and farnesane—at ambient pressures up to 5 atmospheres, along with helium dilution. Droplet burning rates, flame dynamics, droplet extinction diameters, and flame radiant output were measured.
research_category: Microgravity Droplet Combustion / Low-Temperature Hydrocarbon Chemistry
combustion_phenomena: Two-stage and three-stage droplet combustion (hot flame, warm flame, cool flame)
Radiative extinction of hot flames and transition to quasi-steady cool flames
Low-temperature branching kinetics in the Negative Temperature Coefficient (NTC) region
Multiple hot-flame reignition cycles at elevated pressures (>2 atm)
Diffusive/kinetic cool-flame extinction at finite droplet diameter
Soot-shell formation and destabilization at elevated pressures
objectives: Further explore the newly discovered quasi-steady 'cool flames' controlled by low-temperature chemistry in the Negative Temperature Coefficient (NTC) region of n-alkane fuels.

Examine the cool flame combustion behavior of pure n-dodecane, n-dodecane/iso-dodecane fuel mixtures, and farnesane (a renewable jet fuel) over ambient pressures from 0.25 atm (or 0.5 atm tested) up to 5 atm.

Investigate the effects of fuel molecular structure, ambient pressure, fuel mixture composition, and helium dilution on droplet burning rates, flame dynamics, droplet extinction diameters, and flame radiant output.

metadata.mission_relevance_explicitly_supported: Explicitly supported for terrestrial engine technologies (HCCI and RCCI internal combustion engines), renewable biofuel blending, validation of complex chemical kinetic mechanisms, and fuel reformulation for hydrogen production in fuel cells. Requires microgravity on ISS to achieve spherically symmetric burning and long residence times. Spacecraft fire safety is noted only as the focus of the precursor FLEX experiment.
